# Quickstart:
#   mkdir -p ~/archivebox/data && cd ~/archivebox
#   curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ArchiveBox/docker-archivebox/main/docker-compose.yml -o docker-compose.yml
#   docker compose pull
#   docker compose up -d --wait
#   Open http://admin.archivebox.localhost:5797/admin/ and complete setup.
# Docs: https://github.com/ArchiveBox/ArchiveBox/wiki/Docker

services:
    archivebox:
        image: ${ARCHIVEBOX_IMAGE:-archivebox/archivebox:latest}
        restart: unless-stopped
        # Uses the image's server --init command and /health/ healthcheck.
        ports:
            - "${ARCHIVEBOX_PORT:-5797}:5797"
        volumes:
            # Includes the database, config, archive, personas, logs, and Sonic index.
            - ./data:/data
            # Share supervisor sockets with one-off `docker compose run` commands.
            - tmp:/tmp/archivebox
        pids_limit: 2048
        shm_size: "1gb"
        environment:
            - PUID                              # optional numeric UID; defaults to collection owner or 911
            - PGID                              # optional numeric GID; defaults to collection group or 911
            - BASE_URL                          # optional canonical URL; otherwise set by the first-run wizard
            - SERVER_SECURITY_MODE              # optional override; defaults to auto
            - PUBLIC_ADD_VIEW=False
            # - ADMIN_USERNAME=admin             # optional unattended first-run admin creation
            # - ADMIN_PASSWORD=[REDACTED]
            # Other options belong in data/ArchiveBox.conf or Personas in the admin UI.
        # To enable the optional noVNC service below, uncomment this dependency too.
        # depends_on:
        #     novnc:
        #         condition: service_healthy

    # The main server runs queued captures and database-backed scheduled crawls.
    # No scheduler sidecar or restart is needed after adding a schedule:
    #   docker compose exec archivebox archivebox schedule --add --every=day --depth=1 'https://example.com/feed.xml'
    # Sonic also runs inside the main container, with its index in /data/sonic.
    # Rebuild search indexes for existing content:
    #   docker compose exec archivebox archivebox update --index-only

    # Optional browser viewing/control. Uncomment this service and depends_on above.
    # The image discovers novnc:0.0 automatically; profiles stay in /data/personas.
    # Set ARCHIVEBOX_VNC_PERSONA in archivebox.environment to choose a persona.
    # Visit http://127.0.0.1:8080/vnc.html (noVNC has no authentication).
    # novnc:
    #     image: theasp/novnc:latest
    #     restart: unless-stopped
    #     environment:
    #         - DISPLAY_WIDTH=1920
    #         - DISPLAY_HEIGHT=1080
    #         - RUN_XTERM=no
    #     healthcheck:
    #         test: ["CMD", "xdpyinfo", "-display", ":0"]
    #         interval: 2s
    #         timeout: 2s
    #         retries: 10
    #     ports:
    #         - "127.0.0.1:8080:8080"

# Optional remote archive storage: see README.md for host-mounted S3/B2/R2,
# NFS/SMB, or the Rclone Docker volume plugin. Mount only /data/archive remotely;
# keep SQLite, personas, logs, and the Sonic index on local storage.
volumes:
    tmp:

services:
  gatus:
    image: twinproduction/gatus:v5.37.0
    restart: unless-stopped
    env_file: .env
    volumes:
      - ./config.yaml:/config/config.yaml:ro
      - ./data:/data
    ports:
      - 127.0.0.1:18081:8080
    cpus: 0.5
    mem_limit: 512m
  nginx:
    image: nginx:stable-alpine
    restart: unless-stopped
    volumes:
      - ./nginx.conf:/etc/nginx/conf.d/default.conf:ro
      - ./public:/usr/share/nginx/html:ro
    ports:
      - 127.0.0.1:18080:80
    depends_on: [gatus]
    cpus: 0.25
    mem_limit: 64m
  argo:
    image: cloudflare/cloudflared:2026.10.0
    command: tunnel --no-autoupdate --config /etc/cloudflared/config.yml run
    volumes:
      - ./etc/cloudflared:/etc/cloudflared:ro
    restart: unless-stopped
    depends_on: [nginx]
    cpus: 0.5
    mem_limit: 256m

# ArchiveBox Docker deployments

Deployment examples for the stable [ArchiveBox](https://github.com/ArchiveBox/ArchiveBox) `latest` image. The image includes the web server, crawl orchestrator, Sonic, and extraction dependencies. One server container manages each collection, including scheduled crawls and jobs submitted through the UI/API.

- [Docker Compose](docker-compose.yml) — recommended single-host deployment
- [Kubernetes](archivebox.yml) — single-replica example
- [Image Dockerfile](https://github.com/ArchiveBox/ArchiveBox/blob/main/Dockerfile) and [upstream Compose](https://github.com/ArchiveBox/ArchiveBox/blob/main/docker-compose.yml)
- [Docker documentation](https://github.com/ArchiveBox/ArchiveBox/wiki/Docker), [configuration](https://github.com/ArchiveBox/ArchiveBox/wiki/Configuration), and [releases](https://github.com/ArchiveBox/ArchiveBox/releases)

## Quickstart

Requires Docker Engine or Docker Desktop with Docker Compose v2. Images support `linux/amd64` and `linux/arm64` (including Apple Silicon); 32-bit ARM/x86 are unsupported.

```bash
mkdir -p ~/archivebox/data && cd ~/archivebox
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ArchiveBox/docker-archivebox/main/docker-compose.yml -o docker-compose.yml
docker compose pull
docker compose up -d --wait
```

Open [the admin setup wizard](http://admin.archivebox.localhost:5797/admin/). For a remote server, use its hostname or IP and `/admin/`. The wizard configures the canonical URL and security mode; `BASE_URL` and `SERVER_SECURITY_MODE` can override them. Optional `ADMIN_USERNAME` and `ADMIN_PASSWORD` create an administrator without the interactive wizard.

The image's default command is `archivebox server --init 0.0.0.0:5797`; initialization is automatic. It also supplies the `/health/` healthcheck. Set `ARCHIVEBOX_PORT` in `.env` to change the host port; the container still listens on 5797.

```bash
docker compose exec archivebox archivebox version
docker compose exec archivebox archivebox add --depth=1 'https://example.com'
docker compose exec -T archivebox archivebox add < ~/Downloads/bookmarks.txt
docker compose exec archivebox archivebox status
docker compose logs -f archivebox
```

Use `exec archivebox archivebox ...` with a running server, or `run --rm archivebox ...` for a one-off container. The Compose `tmp` volume shares supervisor sockets between these containers. Only run one server/orchestrator per collection.

Without Compose:

```bash
mkdir -p ~/archivebox/data && cd ~/archivebox
docker run -d --name archivebox --restart unless-stopped \
    --pids-limit 2048 --shm-size 1g \
    -p 5797:5797 -v "$PWD/data:/data" \
    archivebox/archivebox:latest
docker exec -it archivebox archivebox status
```

## Persistent data and configuration

### Automatically follow the dev image on Linux

For a test deployment in `/opt/archivebox` using `archivebox/archivebox:dev`, install
the [systemd service](systemd/archivebox-dev-image.service) and
[timer](systemd/archivebox-dev-image.timer) in `/etc/systemd/system/`, then run:

```bash
sudo systemctl daemon-reload
sudo systemctl enable --now archivebox-dev-image.timer
```

The timer checks every two minutes, preserves Compose overrides, and recreates
only the ArchiveBox service when its image changes. Before pulling and after
recreating, it removes only dangling images labeled with ArchiveBox's canonical
source URL; tagged images and images referenced by containers are retained. It
then waits for the container's healthcheck. Inspect failures with
`journalctl -u archivebox-dev-image.service`. Adjust the service's
`WorkingDirectory` for a different deployment location. Use this for deployments
intended to track development builds automatically.

### Pause a small host before disk exhaustion

The optional host disk guard stops the ArchiveBox container below **2 GiB** free
on any monitored filesystem and resumes it at **2.1 GiB**. It records the exact
container and its restart policy, disables Docker automatic restarts while
paused (including after a reboot), and never starts an unrelated or manually
stopped container. It cancels an active image updater when the reserve is crossed;
updates require 2.1 GiB both before pulling and before recreating the container.

Install from this checkout on the Docker host:

```bash
sudo install -m 755 bin/archivebox-disk-guard /usr/local/sbin/archivebox-disk-guard
sudo install -m 644 systemd/archivebox-disk-guard.{service,timer} /etc/systemd/system/
sudo mkdir -p /etc/systemd/system/archivebox-dev-image.service.d
sudo install -m 644 systemd/archivebox-dev-image-disk-guard.conf /etc/systemd/system/archivebox-dev-image.service.d/disk-guard.conf
sudo systemctl daemon-reload
sudo systemctl enable --now archivebox-disk-guard.timer
sudo systemctl start archivebox-disk-guard.service
```

The five-second check monitors `/`, `/var/lib/docker`, and
`/opt/archivebox/data`, plus `/var/lib/containerd` when present. Set
`DEPLOYMENT_DIR` and a space-separated `DISK_PATHS` in
`/etc/default/archivebox-disk-guard` when these paths differ. The guard stores its
pause record under `/var/lib/archivebox-disk-guard`. Inspect transitions with
`journalctl -u archivebox-disk-guard.service`; it gracefully stops the whole
ArchiveBox container, so the web UI also becomes unavailable while paused.
Other host services remain running. Sampling and the 60-second graceful shutdown
cannot guarantee a reserve against a sudden large write or unrelated writers.
The guard stops writes; it does not delete data to make space.

The single `./data:/data` bind mount includes:

| Path | Contents |
| --- | --- |
| `data/index.sqlite3` | Collection database and scheduled crawls |
| `data/ArchiveBox.conf` | Collection configuration |
| `data/archive/` | Saved snapshot files |
| `data/personas/` | Persona configuration, cookies, and browser profiles |
| `data/sonic/` | Local Sonic search index and generated configuration |
| `data/logs/` | Application and worker logs |

Personas always live under `data/personas`; no separate profile volume is needed. `/tmp/archivebox` is runtime state, not a backup of your collection. Keep the database, personas, logs, and search index on reliable local storage. Only `data/archive` may be mounted remotely.

The entrypoint uses the collection owner's numeric UID/GID, falling back to 911. Set `PUID` and `PGID` when the mounted filesystem requires specific IDs, and make both local data and remote archive storage writable by those IDs.

Use the admin Personas UI or `ArchiveBox.conf` for capture configuration. Environment settings override collection configuration; `PUBLIC_ADD_VIEW=False` keeps anonymous submission disabled. Configure access and sharing through the setup wizard rather than copying old wildcard host/CSRF settings. For HTTPS, place your preferred reverse proxy in front of port 5797 and set the externally reachable `BASE_URL`.

## Scheduling and search

```bash
docker compose exec archivebox archivebox schedule --add --every=day --depth=1 'https://example.com/feed.xml'
docker compose exec archivebox archivebox schedule --show
```

The running server picks up database-backed schedules automatically. There is no separate scheduler container or cron restart step.

Sonic is included and managed inside the main container by default, listening on loopback. No separate Sonic service, published 1491 port, or downloaded `sonic.cfg` is needed. Its current configuration keys are `SEARCH_BACKEND_SONIC_*`; remove old overrides pointing at a `sonic` sidecar. `SEARCH_BACKEND_SONIC_ENABLED` controls the plugin, and `SEARCH_BACKEND_ENGINE` chooses the query backend.

To rebuild indexes from existing saved content:

```bash
docker compose exec archivebox archivebox update --index-only
```

## S3, B2, R2, and other remote archive storage

Mount remote storage at **`/data/archive` only**. SQLite and browser profiles must remain local. The snapshot tree contains `users/<user>/snapshots/...` plus legacy timestamp symlinks: Rclone mounts need `--vfs-links`, and file transfers need `--links` to preserve those links.

### Host-mounted storage

On a Linux Docker host, configure a remote with `rclone config`, install FUSE, and enable `user_allow_other` in `/etc/fuse.conf`. For example, mount an S3 remote named `archivebox-s3` at an existing, empty host directory:

```bash
mkdir -p /mnt/archivebox-archive
rclone mount archivebox-s3:BUCKET/archive /mnt/archivebox-archive \
    --allow-other --uid 911 --gid 911 \
    --vfs-cache-mode full --vfs-links
```

Run this under a service manager with a persistent local VFS cache; match UID/GID to your collection. Start the mount before ArchiveBox and verify it is mounted after host restarts. Docker Desktop runs its daemon in a VM, so a host FUSE mount is not automatically equivalent to a Linux Docker-host mount.

For systemd, use `Type=notify` so rclone signals readiness only after its VFS cache
has loaded. Install [rclone-mount-readiness.conf](systemd/rclone-mount-readiness.conf)
as `/etc/systemd/system/YOUR-MOUNT.service.d/readiness.conf`, then run
`systemctl daemon-reload`. Large caches can take longer than systemd's default
90-second startup deadline to scan; repeatedly killing that scan prevents the
mount from ever becoming ready. This drop-in lets the scan finish without a fixed
startup deadline. Keep the ArchiveBox service ordered after and dependent on the
mount, and keep its mountpoint check; never start captures on the empty directory
underneath an unready mount. Inspect startup with `journalctl -u YOUR-MOUNT.service`.

Add this entry alongside the existing `/data` and `/tmp/archivebox` volumes:

```yaml
            - type: bind
              source: /mnt/archivebox-archive
              target: /data/archive
              bind:
                  create_host_path: false
```

`create_host_path: false` catches a missing directory; it does not detect an unmounted filesystem. Stop ArchiveBox if the mount fails, and recreate its container after remounting. The same nested bind-mount layout works for host-mounted NFS/SMB storage.

See [Rclone mount/cache options](https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_mount/) and [ArchiveBox storage setup](https://github.com/ArchiveBox/ArchiveBox/wiki/Setting-up-Storage) for provider configuration and service setup.

### Rclone Docker volume plugin

Alternatively, on Linux Docker Engine, install the [Rclone volume plugin](https://rclone.org/docker/) for your architecture (`amd64` or `arm64`). Install FUSE on the Docker host and place your provider credentials in its protected config file:

```bash
sudo mkdir -p /var/lib/docker-plugins/rclone/config /var/lib/docker-plugins/rclone/cache
sudo install -m 600 ~/.config/rclone/rclone.conf /var/lib/docker-plugins/rclone/config/rclone.conf
docker plugin install rclone/docker-volume-rclone:amd64 --grant-all-permissions --alias rclone
```

Add `- archive:/data/archive` to `services.archivebox.volumes`, and add `archive` alongside the existing `tmp` entry in the top-level `volumes` mapping:

```yaml
volumes:
    tmp:
    archive:
        driver: rclone
        driver_opts:
            remote: 'archivebox-s3:BUCKET/archive'
            allow_other: 'true'
            vfs_cache_mode: full
            vfs_links: 'true'
            uid: '911'
            gid: '911'
```

Use a plugin version that supports `vfs_links`. This is a storage mount; S3 credentials are configured in Rclone, not passed as an ArchiveBox upload backend.

For existing archives, stop writers, back up the collection, copy payloads with `rclone copy --links`, and verify with `rclone check --links` before switching mounts. Keep the original payloads until captures, replay, search, and restart behavior work against the new mount. Mounting an empty bucket over an existing archive hides the local files; it does not migrate them.

## Optional browser access

Uncomment `novnc` and the matching `depends_on` section in Compose. The image detects `novnc:0.0` and opens the selected persona's browser; `ARCHIVEBOX_VNC_PERSONA` chooses a persona (otherwise `DEFAULT_PERSONA`). Visit [noVNC](http://127.0.0.1:8080/vnc.html) to log into sites or watch captures. The browser profile persists in `data/personas`.

The noVNC port is bound to localhost because it has no authentication. For a remote host, use an SSH tunnel. Without noVNC the browser runs headlessly.

## Upgrading an older deployment

1. Back up the entire collection and your old Compose/config files with ArchiveBox stopped. Keep any separate persona volume until its contents are copied into `data/personas` and verified.
2. Stop the old stack, including its scheduler and Sonic services. Replace the Compose file, retaining your data path, port, and intentional configuration overrides.
3. Remove the old Sonic hostname override (`SEARCH_BACKEND_HOST_NAME=sonic` or `SEARCH_BACKEND_SONIC_HOST_NAME=sonic`) from both environment and saved config. The bundled service uses loopback. Keep the old Sonic index backup; rebuild the current index with `update --index-only` if needed.
4. Pull and start the current image. Check health, login, existing snapshots, and a new capture. Recreate legacy cron schedules using `schedule --add`; inspect `schedule --show` to avoid duplicates.

```bash
docker compose pull
docker compose up -d --wait --remove-orphans
docker compose exec archivebox archivebox version
docker compose exec archivebox archivebox schedule --show
```

Do not use `down -v` during an upgrade. Review [collection upgrade guidance](https://github.com/ArchiveBox/ArchiveBox/wiki/Upgrading-or-Merging-Archives) before upgrading older data; retain a pre-upgrade backup for rollback.

## Image versions and development

Docker Compose defaults to `archivebox/archivebox:latest`, following stable releases. Use `dev` explicitly to test release candidates. Set `ARCHIVEBOX_IMAGE` in `.env` to a compatible published version, `sha-<commit>` tag, or digest to pin deployments. Check the [published tags](https://hub.docker.com/r/archivebox/archivebox/tags); arbitrary branch aliases are not guaranteed. Images are also published to `ghcr.io/archivebox/archivebox`.

The production Dockerfile lives in the main ArchiveBox repository and extends the `abx-dl` runtime image. To customize it, extend the complete image rather than installing only the Python package into a bare Python container:

```dockerfile
FROM archivebox/archivebox:dev
# Add your deployment-specific files/configuration here.
```

To build the server image from its canonical checkout:

```bash
cd ../archivebox
./bin/build_docker.sh dev
```

Image publication is handled by the main repository's release workflow after CI; this repository contains deployment definitions only.

## Kubernetes

[archivebox.yml](archivebox.yml) provides a namespace, PVC, single-replica Deployment with `Recreate`, and a ClusterIP Service. Choose a reliable block-backed storage class and sufficient PVC capacity before applying it. SQLite requires filesystem locking/fsync semantics; do not use an NFS/SMB PVC for all of `/data`. Do not scale replicas against one collection.

```bash
kubectl apply -f archivebox.yml
kubectl -n archivebox rollout status deployment/archivebox
kubectl -n archivebox port-forward service/archivebox 5797:5797
```

Open the admin setup wizard as above. For remote access, configure your own Ingress or change the Service to `LoadBalancer`. The image initializes the collection itself; no init container or scheduler/Sonic sidecar is needed. Kubernetes does not use Docker image healthchecks, so the manifest includes startup and readiness probes and a memory-backed `/dev/shm` for Chromium. This example is not part of ArchiveBox's release acceptance matrix; validate it with your storage class and cluster.

# ArchiveBox status on Cabbage

Gatus 5.37.0 runs at https://status.archivebox.io (also
https://archiveboxstatus.zervice.io), deployed in `/opt/archivebox.status`.
The stack follows the neighboring `/opt/archivebox.demo` layout: persistent
bind mounts, resource limits, restart policies, and a dedicated cloudflared tunnel.

All configured public URLs are checked every minute, following redirects and
requiring HTTP 200. API/admin/demo health additionally require `OK`; chat bot
requires JSON `ok: true`. TLSNotary uses `/health`. Image hosting checks a real
existing image because its directory index intentionally returns 403. Brittany
Sweeting, IRC, its web client, and Dunhamfamily are excluded.

Open a service to see native 24h, 7d, and 30d response-time charts. Gatus's SQLite
store retains 30 days of aggregated uptime and latency (hourly recent data,
daily older data), independently of the 100 recent raw check results. This
covers the requested two-week trend without a large dashboard payload. History
started October 12, 2026; no historical results have been fabricated.

The **Cabbage: deployed commit, branch heads & disk space** link opens
`/deployment.html`. It displays the exact running container's OCI revision,
version and image ID, links to the deployed/dev/main commits and comparisons,
and root filesystem available space. Behind/ahead counts are computed against
immutable GitHub commit IDs; a diverged main branch is identified explicitly.
The host collector runs every minute, caches GitHub comparisons for ten minutes,
and refreshes them immediately if the deployed revision changes. GitHub lookup
errors are shown as unknown. The page marks host metadata stale after three
minutes; a Gatus heartbeat also fails when the collector stops updating.

## Deployment

Requires Docker Compose, systemd, bash, curl, jq, and OpenSSL on Cabbage.
Copy this directory to `/opt/archivebox.status`, preserving `.env`, `data/`, and
`etc/cloudflared/`. Keep generated metadata, credentials, and SQLite out of Git.
Only nginx/Gatus bind to loopback; public access goes through Cloudflare.
The host collector uses Docker locally; no container mounts the Docker socket.

```bash
cd /opt/archivebox.status
mkdir -p data public etc/cloudflared
umask 077
test -f .env || printf 'COLLECTOR_TOKEN=%s\n' "$(openssl rand -hex 32)" > .env
install -m 600 -o 65532 -g 65532 \
  /opt/archivebox.demo/etc/cloudflared/cert.pem etc/cloudflared/cert.pem
chown 65532:65532 etc/cloudflared
```

For a new installation, create a named tunnel using the cloudflared Compose
image, then route `archiveboxstatus.zervice.io` to it. The live deployment uses
tunnel `5d662698-3ca7-4694-a22f-a9e800126d4d`. Its
`etc/cloudflared/config.yml` is:

```yaml
tunnel: 5d662698-3ca7-4694-a22f-a9e800126d4d
credentials-file: /etc/cloudflared/5d662698-3ca7-4694-a22f-a9e800126d4d.json
protocol: http2
ingress:
  - hostname: status.archivebox.io
    service: http://nginx:80
  - hostname: archiveboxstatus.zervice.io
    service: http://nginx:80
  - service: http_status:404
```

The `status.archivebox.io` DNS alias points to `archiveboxstatus.zervice.io`.
Do not recreate existing credentials or overwrite DNS routes during updates.

```bash
docker compose config --quiet
docker compose up -d
cp systemd/archivebox-status.* /etc/systemd/system/
systemctl daemon-reload
systemctl enable --now archivebox-status.timer
systemctl start archivebox-status.service
curl -fsS http://127.0.0.1:18080/deployment.json
curl -fsS https://status.archivebox.io/api/v1/endpoints/statuses
```

After replacing a bind-mounted configuration file, restart its service so the
container sees the new inode (`docker compose restart gatus` for config.yaml,
`docker compose restart nginx` for nginx.conf). `public/` is a directory mount,
so the collector's atomic JSON replacement is visible immediately.

Back up `data/gatus.db*`, `.env`, and `etc/cloudflared/` securely. Monitor both
`systemctl status archivebox-status.timer` and `docker compose ps`. This status
page shares Cabbage's availability; it cannot report a total Cabbage outage while
the host is down. No alert destinations are configured.

Host metadata refreshes every minute; GitHub comparisons every 10 minutes and after a deployment. Revision comes from the running container's OCI image label. Monitoring is hosted on Cabbage, so a full host outage also takes this page offline.

---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: archivebox
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata:
  name: archivebox
  namespace: archivebox
spec:
  # Uses the cluster's default StorageClass. Choose reliable block-backed storage;
  # do not put the SQLite database on NFS/SMB. Adjust capacity for your archive.
  accessModes:
    - ReadWriteOnce
  resources:
    requests:
      storage: 20Gi
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: archivebox
  namespace: archivebox
spec:
  replicas: 1
  # One server/orchestrator owns the collection; stop it before replacing it.
  strategy:
    type: Recreate
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: archivebox
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: archivebox
    spec:
      terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 60
      containers:
        - name: archivebox
          image: archivebox/archivebox:dev
          imagePullPolicy: Always
          # Inherit the image's server --init command and privilege-dropping entrypoint.
          ports:
            - containerPort: 5797
              name: http
          env:
            - name: PUBLIC_ADD_VIEW
              value: "False"
            # Set BASE_URL and SERVER_SECURITY_MODE here to override the setup wizard.
          resources:
            requests:
              cpu: 250m
              memory: 1Gi
          startupProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /health/
              port: http
              httpHeaders:
                - name: Host
                  value: admin.archivebox.localhost
            periodSeconds: 10
            timeoutSeconds: 5
            failureThreshold: 60
          readinessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /health/
              port: http
              httpHeaders:
                - name: Host
                  value: admin.archivebox.localhost
            periodSeconds: 10
            timeoutSeconds: 5
          volumeMounts:
            - name: archivebox
              mountPath: /data
            - name: shm
              mountPath: /dev/shm
      volumes:
        - name: archivebox
          persistentVolumeClaim:
            claimName: archivebox
        - name: shm
          emptyDir:
            medium: Memory
            sizeLimit: 1Gi
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: archivebox
  namespace: archivebox
spec:
  type: ClusterIP
  selector:
    app: archivebox
  ports:
    - name: http
      port: 5797
      targetPort: http

storage:
  type: sqlite
  path: /data/gatus.db
  maximum-number-of-results: 100
  maximum-number-of-events: 500
ui:
  title: ArchiveBox Status
  header: ArchiveBox
  link: https://archivebox.io
  dashboard-heading: ArchiveBox service status
  dashboard-subheading: "Checked every minute from Cabbage. Open a service for latency and uptime history (7d / 30d). History begins October 12, 2026."
  default-sort-by: group
  buttons:
    - name: "Cabbage: deployed commit, branch heads & disk space"
      link: /deployment.html
    - name: GitHub
      link: https://github.com/ArchiveBox/ArchiveBox
endpoints:
  - name: API health
    group: Services
    url: https://api.archivebox.io/health/
    interval: 1m
    conditions: ["[STATUS] == 200", "[BODY] == OK", "[RESPONSE_TIME] < 10000"]
  - name: Website
    group: Landing pages
    url: https://archivebox.io/
    interval: 1m
    conditions: ["[STATUS] == 200", "[RESPONSE_TIME] < 10000"]
  - name: Public archive
    group: Services
    url: https://web.archivebox.io/
    interval: 1m
    conditions: ["[STATUS] == 200", "[RESPONSE_TIME] < 15000"]
  - name: Documentation
    group: 3rd party
    url: https://docs.archivebox.io/
    interval: 1m
    conditions: ["[STATUS] == 200", "[RESPONSE_TIME] < 10000"]
  - name: Admin health
    group: Services

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Run on the Docker host; only selected public metadata leaves this script.
set -euo pipefail
cd /opt/archivebox.status
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source .env
mkdir -p public data
now=$(date +%s)
container=archiveboxdemo-archivebox-1
deployed=$(docker inspect "$container" --format '{{index .Config.Labels "org.opencontainers.image.revision"}}')
[[ "$deployed" =~ ^[0-9a-f]{40}$ ]]
version=$(docker inspect "$container" --format '{{index .Config.Labels "org.opencontainers.image.version"}}')
image=$(docker inspect "$container" --format '{{.Image}}')
read -r total available < <(df -B1 --output=size,avail / | tail -1)
branches='{}'
if [[ -f data/branches.json ]]; then branches=$(cat data/branches.json); fi
cached=$(jq -r '.checked_at // 0' <<< "$branches")
cached_commit=$(jq -r '.deployed // ""' <<< "$branches")
if (( now - cached >= 600 )) || [[ "$cached_commit" != "$deployed" ]]; then
    branches=$(jq -n --arg deployed "$deployed" --argjson now "$now" '{deployed:$deployed,checked_at:$now}')
    for branch in dev main; do
        # Resolve the head first, then compare exact immutable commits.
        if head_json=$(curl -fsS --max-time 20 "https://api.github.com/repos/ArchiveBox/ArchiveBox/commits/$branch") &&
           head=$(jq -er '.sha | select(test("^[0-9a-f]{40}$"))' <<< "$head_json") &&
           comparison=$(curl -fsS --max-time 20 "https://api.github.com/repos/ArchiveBox/ArchiveBox/compare/$deployed...$head"); then
            item=$(jq --arg head "$head" '{head:$head,status:.status,behind:.ahead_by,ahead:.behind_by}' <<< "$comparison")
        else
            item='{"error":"GitHub lookup unavailable; comparison unknown"}'
        fi
        branches=$(jq --arg branch "$branch" --argjson item "$item" '.[$branch]=$item' <<< "$branches")
    done
    printf '%s\n' "$branches" > data/branches.json.tmp
    mv data/branches.json.tmp data/branches.json
fi
jq -n --argjson now "$now" --arg deployed "$deployed" --arg version "$version" --arg image "$image" \
  --argjson total "$total" --argjson available "$available" --argjson branches "$branches" \
  '{updated_at:$now,host:"cabbage",deployed:$deployed,version:$version,image:$image,branches:$branches,
    disk:{path:"/",total_bytes:$total,available_bytes:$available,available_gib:(($available/1073741824*10|floor)/10),free_percent:(($available/$total*1000|floor)/10)}}' > public/deployment.json.tmp
chmod 644 public/deployment.json.tmp
mv public/deployment.json.tmp public/deployment.json
# A missed heartbeat is marked failed by Gatus after three minutes.
printf 'header = "Authorization: Bearer %s"\n' "$COLLECTOR_TOKEN" |
    curl --config - -fsS --max-time 15 -X POST \
    'http://127.0.0.1:18081/api/v1/endpoints/cabbage_deployment-collector/external?success=true' >/dev/null
